messages:
jin: quick heads-up — observed a weird kernel pick in the autotuner for v3 on causal workloads. head_dim=30 models are getting routed to the SDPA slowpath instead of the optimized flash path.

sara: repro steps? which GPU arch / seqlen / batch?

jin: SM80, seqlen=512, batch=8, kv_cache enabled; probe logs: `kernel_picker: probing sdpa_v3 (est latency 7.8ms) vs flash_v2 (est 6.1ms)` but actual perf is flipped once kv cache warms.

alex: hmm that sounds like we'll be underestimating the impact of kv cache state on effective head stride. do you have perf traces (pytorch/cuda-nvprof)?

jin: pasted short trace below (from perf-bot run):
```
perf-bot: profile run 1779999999
SM80 | model=head30 | seqlen=512 | batch=8 | kv_cache=hot
flash_v2: 11.2 ms (tail)
sdpa_v3: 9.3 ms (tail)
kernel_picker estimate: flash_v2 6.1ms, sdpa_v3 7.8ms
```

priya: so the picker estimate is stale once kv cache hits and microbatching changes effective memory layout. picker needs to account for kv_cache hit rate and microbatch alignment.

mike: noted. possible fixes: (1) add a cheap online probe that measures a single token hot-kv latency and adjusts scores; (2) bump heuristic weight for head dims not divisible by 8 to prefer sdpa_v3 only when it actually benefits; (3) fall back to short warmup that samples both kernels on first requests.

sara: option (1) seems least invasive. we could piggyback on existing autotuner probe step. question: how noisy will per-request probes be for multi-tenant hosts?

jin: we can aggregate per-route stats for a minute and smooth with EWMA. example pseudo: `score_k = alpha*measured_k + (1-alpha)*estimated_k` where measured_k only updates when kv_hot_ratio > 0.6.

alex: also consider arch-specific behavior: on SM86 flash_v2 wins more often for head%32 cases but on SM80 the sdpa_v3 tiling wins for seqlen>=512 even with awkward head dims. we should encode a small lookup table keyed by (arch, seqlen_bucket, head_mod_8).

perf-bot: suggestion: run batch sweep 1-16 and head_dim 16..64 step=2 on SM80/SM86, cache results to model-profile store. automated job scheduled.

priya: one more gotcha — routing by route/model version means we can pin a model to the better kernel while autotuner collects stats. do we have rollout APIs for kernel pinning?

ops-bot: yes — deploy tool supports per-model kernel overrides via `runtime.config.kernel_preference` (canary flag). use `--role experiment` to limit.

mike: action items: 1) jin to land a small probe hook that measures hot-kv single-token latency (PR). 2) alex to draft arch x seqlen x head_mod table and a fallback policy. 3) perf-bot to run the sweep and upload CSV. 4) priya to add route pin API docs.

jin: i'll start the probe PR today, will attach logs. thanks. :thumbsup:

sara: awesome. if probe shows large variance we may need to weight by p95 not mean. keep us posted.

alex: +1 to p95. also add an opt-out for privacy-sensitive routes (no per-request profiling).

mike: noted. closing loop once sweep completes.

ops-bot: canary deployed autotuner-probe v0.1 to us-west-2 (limited).
